description: A recursive descent parser builds an AST using dataclass nodes (Num, BinOp, UnaryOp) instead of tuples. The parsing logic is unchanged; only the node construction changes. A pretty printer uses structural pattern matching to display the tree.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Dataclass definitions for AST nodes: Num holds a float value; BinOp has op, left, right; UnaryOp has op and operand. These replace the tuple representation like ('+', left, right).
Parser class takes a token list. peek returns current token, advance consumes and returns it, eat asserts token type matches expected.
parse_additive calls parse_multiplicative for left node, then while peek is + or -, advances, parses right, builds BinOp(op, node, right)  -  the fold-left loop for left associativity.

steps.question: What AST node replaces the tuple ('+', node, right) in the old parser?

steps.description: parse_multiplicative mirrors additive for * and /. parse_unary handles leading - by building UnaryOp(op, parse_unary()). parse_primary handles NUM tokens (returning Num) and parenthesized expressions.

pretty uses match/case structural pattern matching on dataclass nodes to print the tree with indentation. Num prints value; BinOp prints op then recurses on children. UnaryOp prints op and recurses on operand.
Demo tokens for '3 + -(2 * 4)' parse to AST: BinOp('+') with Num(3) and UnaryOp('-') wrapping BinOp('*') with Num(2) and Num(4).

title: Parser Upgrade: Tuples to Dataclass AST Nodes
